name: Masala Pasta
steps: Check that the dry penne is eggless. Boil 2200 ml water with 8 g salt in a large pot. Add the pasta, stir well and cook until just al dente, following the packet time. Reserve 150 ml cooking water, then drain the pasta without rinsing it. Meanwhile finely chop the onion, tomatoes, ginger, garlic and chilli; dice the bell pepper and carrot into small, even pieces.

Heat 30 ml oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes until softened and lightly golden. Add ginger, garlic and green chilli; stir for 1 minute until fragrant. Add diced carrot and peas with 50 ml reserved pasta water, cover and cook for 4 minutes until the carrot starts to soften.

Stir in turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder for 20 seconds. Add chopped tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook uncovered for 7–9 minutes, stirring and pressing the tomatoes, until they break down into a thick, cohesive masala and the raw tomato smell fades. Add the bell pepper and cook for 2 minutes so it stays slightly crisp.

Fold the drained penne into the masala with 50–100 ml reserved pasta water, adding only enough to coat every piece without making the sauce watery. Add garam masala and the remaining 4 g salt, then simmer together for 2 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning; the finished pasta should be moist and well coated, not swimming in sauce.
Turn off the heat, scatter chopped coriander leaves over the pasta and serve hot in four bowls. Divide the visible peas, carrot and bell pepper evenly among the servings.
tips: The reviewed dish photo shows red onion-tomato masala clinging to penne with peas, green bell pepper, carrot and coriander. Keep this as a savory Indian masala pasta, without cream or cheese. Reserve pasta water before draining so the masala coats the pasta evenly.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
